subject: Urban Planning
title: Accessory Commercial Units
description: Learn Accessory Commercial Units in one minute.

hook.text: In most American neighborhoods, running a small business from home is illegal. Zoning says residential means residential.

buildup.text: Home occupations are technically allowed in some zones but with extreme limits: no customers, no signage, no employees.

discovery.text: Before zoning, every neighborhood had a corner store, a tailor, a barber. They made communities walkable.

twist.text: COVID forced millions to work from home. Zoning codes written for commuter lifestyles suddenly made no sense.

climax.text: Some cities now allow 'accessory commercial units' — small shops in garages or front rooms. The corner store returns.

punchline.text: The corner store is illegal in most neighborhoods. We wonder why we drive everywhere.

quiz.question: Why are small neighborhood businesses rare in American suburbs?
options: Suburban residents don't want shops near their homes
Zoning codes ban commercial uses in residential areas
Insurance costs make small businesses unviable in suburbs
